source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 5 (Indian Theatre and Drama Traditions).

sections.heading: 1. Roots of Indian Theatre
points: Indian theatre traces back to the **Natyashastra of Bharata Muni** — sometimes called the 'fifth Veda'; it defines **natya** and the concept of **rasa**.
Classical **Sanskrit drama** flourished with playwrights like **Bhasa, Kalidasa (Abhijnana Shakuntalam), Shudraka (Mrichchhakatika), Vishakhadatta, Bhavabhuti**.
Theatre combined dialogue, music, dance and gesture.

sections.heading: 2. Traditional/Folk Theatre Forms
points: **Kutiyattam** (Kerala) — the oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre; a **UNESCO ICH**.
**Ramlila** (North India) — dramatic enactment of the Ramayana; a **UNESCO ICH**.

**Yakshagana** (Karnataka), **Bhavai** (Gujarat), **Tamasha** (Maharashtra), **Nautanki** (North India), **Jatra** (Bengal), **Bhaona/Ankia Naat** (Assam — Sankaradeva), **Therukoothu** (Tamil Nadu), **Swang, Bhand Pather** (Kashmir).
These are open-air, community forms mixing narration, song and comedy.

sections.heading: 3. Puppet-linked and Devotional Theatre
points: Many forms are **religious/devotional** (Ramlila, Raslila for Krishna).
**Bhaona** (Assam) grew from the Vaishnava Bhakti movement of **Sankaradeva**.
Theatre served as **entertainment, moral teaching and social commentary**.

sections.heading: 4. Modern Indian Theatre
points: Modern theatre developed under colonial and Western influence (proscenium stage).
Institutions: the **National School of Drama (NSD)**, Sangeet Natak Akademi.
Playwrights/directors like **Girish Karnad, Habib Tanvir, Vijay Tendulkar, Badal Sarkar** revived and modernised Indian theatre, often drawing on folk forms.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Natyashastra (Bharata Muni) = source of theatre and the rasa theory.
Kalidasa = Abhijnana Shakuntalam; Shudraka = Mrichchhakatika.
Kutiyattam (Kerala, oldest Sanskrit theatre) and Ramlila = UNESCO ICH.
Yakshagana = Karnataka; Tamasha = Maharashtra; Jatra = Bengal; Bhaona = Assam (Sankaradeva).
National School of Drama (NSD) = premier modern theatre institution.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Kutiyattam (Kerala)** is the **oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre** and a **UNESCO ICH**.
**Ramlila** is also a **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage**.
**Yakshagana = Karnataka**; **Tamasha = Maharashtra**; **Jatra = Bengal**.
The **Natyashastra** gives the **rasa** theory of aesthetics.
